extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and researchers interested in comedy/entertainment
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive Wikipedia biography and career overview of American comedian and actor Patton Oswalt, covering early life, influences, career highlights, topics, outputs, and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Observational comedy; black comedy; insult comedy; sarcasm; satire; deadpan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the article's infobox as the primary comedic styles associated with Oswalt; indicates the stylistic categories his work is commonly assigned to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: American culture; American politics; human behavior; pop culture; current events; religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics Oswalt frequently addresses in his stand-up and other work, presented in the infobox as the recurring thematic material of his comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declared performance media for Oswalt's career, showing the formats in which his comedic work appears (live, TV, cinema).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stand-up content scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Oswalt's stand-up covers topics ranging from pop culture frivolity (comic book supervillains, 1980s glam metal) to deeper social issues like American excess, materialism, foreign policy, and religion; he also discusses his atheism and clinical depression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative in the 'Career' section describing the balance of light/pop-culture material and serious personal/social topics; indicates subject-matter expectations and how personal experience informs material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Influences include Jonathan Winters, Richard Pryor, Emo Philips, Blaine Capatch, Jim Goad, Bill Hicks, Bobcat Goldthwait, Sam Kinison, Steve Martin, and Louis C.K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of comedians and performers cited as shaping Oswalt's comedic voice and approach; useful for contextualizing stylistic lineage and reference points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable roles and career milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Acting/voice roles and milestones such as Spence Olchin on The King of Queens; narrator of The Goldbergs; voice of Remy in Ratatouille; roles in numerous TV series and films; began performing stand-up on July 18, 1988.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chronology and examples in the 'Career' section demonstrating major career achievements and role types that mark professional progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative outputs (specials, albums, books, comics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Six stand-up specials; comedy albums (e.g., Werewolves and Lollipops; My Weakness Is Strong; Talking for Clapping); nonfiction books (Zombie Spaceship Wasteland; Silver Screen Fiend); comics writing credits (JLA: Welcome to the Working Week, Black Hammer: Visions, Minor Threats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated works in 'Discography' and 'Writing' sections that serve as concrete deliverables representing his body of work across media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and nominations as performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Achievements including a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Variety Special and a Grammy Award for Best Comedy Album, plus multiple nominations (Emmys, Grammys, Critics' awards, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Awards and nominations' section lists honors used as indicators of industry recognition and success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public positions and personal life as contextual factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal details and public positions such as being an outspoken atheist, progressive political endorsements (Obama, Biden), activism (PETA), history of clinical depression, and the death of his first wife Michelle McNamara.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biographical details in 'Personal life' that inform public persona and occasionally the content/tone of his comedy; relevant when assessing authenticity or topical material in his work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional affiliations and industry activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities such as writing for MADtv, participating in WGA actions (firing agents during WGA-ATA stand), moderating panels, and involvement in comics and voice acting projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Career activities and industry engagement described in the article that reflect professional standing, community involvement, and cross-medium participation.
